entry_state: Late collateral receipts belong in loss measurement and do not become a separately owned asset. Revolving capacity preserves credit history; fee purpose determines yield or service timing. Partial transfer now requires identifying the eligible asset portion.
exit_state: Partial derecognition allocates carrying value by relative fair values, not nominal principal. Retained risk can require a financing liability; continuing guarantee involvement retains both asset and liability until supported satisfaction or expiry.
findings: The eligible transfer allocates 45 and 55, yielding gain 1 on consideration 46; the nominal 40 percent shortcut would produce the wrong gain 6.
Retaining substantially all risk keeps the asset and recognises a liability for proceeds. The identical receipt does not establish sale.
Guarantee involvement preserves net assets 100 at transfer, 99 after service and loss measurement, and 103 only after the admitted no-claim expiry. No new defect observed.
